name: com.scrapeunblocker/scrapeunblocker-mcp-remote
description: Web search and content extraction for AI: Google results, any page as Markdown or JSON

tools.name: fetch_html
tools.description: Fetch the fully rendered HTML of any public web page through the ScrapeUnblocker API (https://docs.scrapeunblocker.com). The page loads in a real browser, so JavaScript-rendered pages come back complete. Use it when you need the page markup, or when a plain HTTP fetch returns 403/429 or an empty page. Returns raw HTML.

proxy_country.description: Optional ISO country code to route through, e.g. 'US'.

sleep_seconds.description: Extra seconds to wait after load.

tools.name: browse_page
tools.description: Load a web page in a real browser through the ScrapeUnblocker API (https://docs.scrapeunblocker.com), run ordered browser actions on it (click, type into a search box, choose an option, press a key, scroll, wait), then return the resulting HTML. Steps act on the website and are NOT idempotent - they run once per call and are not retried. A failed step returns which step failed plus the page HTML at that point. Billed as one request.

selector.description: CSS selector the action targets (required for wait_for/click/type/select).

value.description: Action payload: text to type/select, text for wait_for_text, a key name for press_key (e.g. 'Enter'), milliseconds for wait, or 'bottom'/pixels for scroll.

steps.description: Ordered browser actions to run after the page loads (wait_for, wait_for_text, wait, click, type [human-like], select, press_key, scroll), then the HTML is captured.

proxy_country.description: Optional ISO country code to route through, e.g. 'US'.

wait_method.description: Optional render-wait before the steps: 'css' selector or 'js' expression.

sleep_seconds.description: Extra seconds to wait after load.

tools.name: capture_xhr
tools.description: Load a web page in a real browser through the ScrapeUnblocker API (https://docs.scrapeunblocker.com) and return the JSON its own API calls received: every XHR/fetch response whose URL contains `capture_xhr` (a fragment such as '/api/search'), in order, with status and body. Use it when a site renders from a JSON API that refuses direct requests: the page makes the call, so it succeeds. Optional `steps` make the page fire the call (a search, 'load more'); steps act on the website and run once. Up to 20 responses; the page HTML is not returned. Billed as one request; when the site refuses every matching call (403/429) the call fails and is free.

capture_xhr.description: A fragment of the API URL the page calls, e.g. '/api/search' (plain substring).

steps.description: Optional browser actions that make the page fire the call. Runs once.

selector.description: CSS selector the action targets (required for wait_for/click/type/select).

value.description: Action payload: text to type/select, text for wait_for_text, a key name for press_key (e.g. 'Enter'), milliseconds for wait, or 'bottom'/pixels for scroll.

proxy_country.description: Optional ISO country code to route through, e.g. 'US'.

tools.name: fetch_parsed
tools.description: Fetch a web page through the ScrapeUnblocker API (https://docs.scrapeunblocker.com) and return AI-parsed structured JSON instead of raw HTML (product details, article content, listings). If the page holds no structured data, the result says so and returns the rendered HTML instead (billed like fetch_html).

url.description: The absolute URL to fetch and parse.

proxy_country.description: Optional ISO country code, e.g. 'US'.

tools.name: google_search
tools.description: Run a Google search through the ScrapeUnblocker API (https://docs.scrapeunblocker.com) and return the results page as JSON: organic results with their real URLs, favicons, sitelinks and star ratings, ads, the AI Overview, People also ask, related searches with their links, the knowledge panel, top stories, videos, local and shopping results. Set `full_urls` when you need the exact page URL of every result.

proxy_country.description: Optional ISO country code to search from, e.g. 'US'.

pages_to_check.description: How many result pages to collect (default 1).

full_urls.description: Wait until Google gives out every result's real URL. Set it when you need the exact page URL of all results (e.g. to cite or open them); leave it off for quick answers. Google releases a results page's links a few at a time, the last ones up to about 40 seconds after the search: without it a result whose link has not come yet has the site's home page as its `url` (or a Google redirect link), with it the call takes up to about 40 seconds longer. Billed the same.

tools.name: list_elements
tools.description: Fetch a page through the ScrapeUnblocker API (https://docs.scrapeunblocker.com) and return its interactive elements (buttons, inputs, selects, links, forms), each with a ready-to-use selector, as JSON {url, count, elements:[...]} instead of raw HTML. Use it to find the selectors a page's buttons, inputs and links answer to.

url.description: The absolute URL to load and inspect (http/https).

proxy_country.description: Optional ISO country code to route through, e.g. 'US'.

sleep_seconds.description: Extra seconds to wait after load before inspecting.

tools.name: fetch_markdown
tools.description: Fetch a web page in a real browser through the ScrapeUnblocker API (https://docs.scrapeunblocker.com) and return it as clean Markdown: the main content with absolute links, without scripts, styles, navigation or footer. Use it to read, quote or summarise a page; it is usually 2-25% the size of the HTML. Works on JavaScript-rendered pages and on pages that return 403/429 to a plain HTTP fetch. Billed as one request.

proxy_country.description: Optional ISO country code to route through, e.g. 'US'.

sleep_seconds.description: Extra seconds to wait after load.

main_content_only.description: Drop navigation, page header, footer and sidebars (default true). False keeps the whole page.

tools.name: search_and_read
tools.description: Search Google through the ScrapeUnblocker API (https://docs.scrapeunblocker.com) and read the top results in one call: returns Google's AI Overview when there is one, each of the first `results` pages (default 3, max 5) as Markdown, and the other organic results as title, URL and snippet. Use it to answer a question from the live web. Billed as one request for the search plus one per page read.

proxy_country.description: Optional ISO country code to search from and read the pages through, e.g. 'US'.

results.description: How many top results to read (default 3, max 5).

tools.name: list_plugins
tools.description: List ScrapeUnblocker's ready-made site plugins: scrapers for specific sites that return clean structured JSON (Amazon, Walmart, Target, eBay, Zillow, Redfin, Booking.com, Airbnb, Indeed, Glassdoor, Google Trends / Shopping / Maps, YouTube, Spotify, App Store, Google Play, Trustpilot, Yelp, Ahrefs, Semrush and 100+ more). A plugin returns a site's data already parsed. Without arguments it lists every plugin with its parameters (* = required); `category` or `search` narrow the list; `name` returns one plugin's full parameter docs. Free - it calls nothing.

name.description: A plugin name, for its full parameter docs.

search.description: Only plugins whose name or description mentions this, e.g. 'zillow' or 'reviews'.

tools.name: run_plugin
tools.description: Run one ScrapeUnblocker site plugin and return its JSON - e.g. a Target or Walmart search, a Zillow listing search, Google Trends for some keywords, an app's App Store reviews. `params` uses the plugin's own parameter names (snake_case); a list value is fine where a parameter takes several. Each run is billed like an API request; listing plugins bill one unit per result page they fetch, so max_results sets the cost.

name.description: The plugin to run, by its plugin name.

tools.name: amazon_search
tools.description: Searches any regional Amazon marketplace for `keyword` and returns the result cards as JSON: `asin`, `title`, `price` + `currency`, `listPrice`, `rating`, `reviewCount`, a clean product `url`, `image`, and the `sponsored` / `prime` flags. Filter with `min_price` / `max_price`, order with `sort` (featured, price_asc, price_desc, avg_review, newest), and page with `page`. Fetch each result's full detail (all fields above plus features and images) through `POST /marketplace/amazon-product`. Some cards show no price on the search page (Amazon defers it, or the item has buying options); those return `price: null` and are kept in the list rather than dropped. `proxy_country` defaults to the marketplace's home country so prices are in the expected currency. Returns JSON. Billed like an API request; listing plugins bill one unit per result page they fetch, so keep max_results modest.

keyword.description: Search phrase, e.g. 'wireless headphones' or a brand + model.

marketplace.description: Regional Amazon site to search. Prices and currency differ per marketplace. One of: amazon.com, amazon.co.uk, amazon.de, amazon.fr, amazon.it, amazon.es, amazon.nl, amazon.se, amazon.pl, amazon.com.be, amazon.com.tr, amazon.ca, amazon.com.mx, amazon.com.br, amazon.co.jp, amazon.in, amazon.ae, amazon.sa, amazon.sg, amazon.com.au. Default: amazon.com.

sort.description: Result order: featured, price_asc, price_desc, avg_review, newest. Default 'featured'. Default: featured.

min_price.description: Lowest price to include, in the marketplace's currency.

max_price.description: Highest price to include, in the marketplace's currency.

proxy_country.description: Proxy country the request is sent from (ISO-2, e.g. 'US', 'DE'). Defaults to the marketplace's home country so prices come back in the expected currency.

tools.name: amazon_product
tools.description: Fetches a single Amazon product and returns it as JSON: `title`, `brand` and `brandStoreUrl`, `parentAsin`, `manufacturer`, `modelNumber`, `partNumber`, `productCodes` (UPC, EAN, GTIN, ISBN), `condition`, the `amazonsChoice`, `bestSellerBadge`, `deal` and `coupon` markers, `price` + `currency`, `listPrice`, `savingsPercent` and `savingsAmount`, `unitPrice`, `subscribeAndSavePrice`, `shippingPrice`, `recentSales`, `availability` (+ a boolean `inStock`), `maxOrderQuantity`, `rating`, `reviewCount`, `ratingDistribution` (percent per star), `reviewSummary`, `seller`, `sellerUrl`, `sellerId`, `shipsFrom`, `fulfilledByAmazon`, `prime`, `delivery`, `returnPolicy`, `offersCount` and `offersFromPrice`, `bestSellersRank`, `features` (bullet points), `categories` (breadcrumb), `description`, `fromTheManufacturer` and `fromTheBrand` (text and images), `importantInformation`, `ingredients`, `whatsInTheBox`, `documents`, `warrantyAndSupport`, `productDetails`, `productOverview`, `dimensions`, `weight`, `dateFirstAvailable`, `variantDimensions` and `variants` (each with its own ASIN and options), `sustainability`, `protectionPlans`, `newerModel`, `sponsoredProducts`, `relatedProducts`, `images` (the whole gallery) and `videos`. A field the page does not show is null or empty. Identify the product with either `asin` (plus `marketplace`) or a full product `url`. Other sellers' full offers are not on the product page: only their count and lowest price are returned here, `/marketplace/amazon-offers` lists them. `prime` and `delivery` are what a visitor who is not signed in sees. Amazon prices each page in the currency of the delivery location it infers from the visitor's IP address, so `proxy_country` defaults to the marketplace's home country (amazon.com -> US) and the call is routed through proxies in that country. The country of the proxy that served the request is reported as `exitCountry`. Returns JSON. Billed like an API request; listing plugins bill one unit per result page they fetch, so keep max_results modest.

asin.description: Amazon product id (10-char ASIN, e.g. 'B0BSHF7WHW'; books use their ISBN-10). Give either `asin` (with `marketplace`) or a full `url`.

url.description: Full Amazon product url, e.g. 'https://www.amazon.de/dp/B0BSHF7WHW'. The ASIN and marketplace are read from it, so `asin`/`marketplace` are not needed when a url is given.

marketplace.description: Regional Amazon site the ASIN belongs to. Prices and currency differ per marketplace. One of: amazon.com, amazon.co.uk, amazon.de, amazon.fr, amazon.it, amazon.es, amazon.nl, amazon.se, amazon.pl, amazon.com.be, amazon.com.tr, amazon.ca, amazon.com.mx, amazon.com.br, amazon.co.jp, amazon.in, amazon.ae, amazon.sa, amazon.sg, amazon.com.au. Default: amazon.com.

proxy_country.description: Proxy country the request is sent from (ISO-2, e.g. 'US', 'DE'). Defaults to the marketplace's home country so the price comes back in the expected currency.

tools.name: amazon_reviews
tools.description: Returns the review data an Amazon product page shows to a signed-out visitor, as JSON: the overall `rating`, total `reviewCount` (global ratings), the 5..1-star `histogram` (percent per star), the AI `customersSay` summary (overall text plus per-aspect `sentiment`, `mentions`, `positive`, `negative`, `summary` and the quoted review `excerpts` Amazon shows for the aspect) and the top `reviews` (each with `id`, `url`, `author`, `rating`, `title`, `body`, `date`, `country`, `fromOtherCountry`, `verified`, `helpfulVotes`, `variant` and `images`). Identify the product with `asin` (plus `marketplace`) or a product `url`. Scope: Amazon only shows its full review list to signed-in customers, so this endpoint returns the public slice on the product page - typically 5 to 13 top reviews, local ones first and then reviews from other countries - not a complete review export. When Amazon hides the top reviews behind a sign-in prompt (common on amazon.com), `reviewsGated` is `true` and `reviews` is empty; the rating, histogram and customers-say data, including its review excerpts, are still returned. Every field is always present and is `null` when the page does not show it. `proxy_country` defaults to the marketplace's home country; the country of the proxy that served the request is reported as `exitCountry`. Returns JSON. Billed like an API request; listing plugins bill one unit per result page they fetch, so keep max_results modest.

asin.description: Amazon product id (10-char ASIN, e.g. 'B07PXGQC1Q'; books use their ISBN-10). Give either `asin` (with `marketplace`) or a product `url`.

url.description: Full Amazon product url, e.g. 'https://www.amazon.de/dp/B0D1XD1ZV3'. The ASIN and marketplace are read from it, so `asin`/`marketplace` are not needed when a url is given.

marketplace.description: Regional Amazon site the ASIN belongs to. Reviews are read from that store. One of: amazon.com, amazon.co.uk, amazon.de, amazon.fr, amazon.it, amazon.es, amazon.nl, amazon.se, amazon.pl, amazon.com.be, amazon.com.tr, amazon.ca, amazon.com.mx, amazon.com.br, amazon.co.jp, amazon.in, amazon.ae, amazon.sa, amazon.sg, amazon.com.au. Default: amazon.com.

proxy_country.description: Proxy country the request is sent from (ISO-2, e.g. 'US', 'DE'). Defaults to the marketplace's home country. The reviews come from the marketplace itself, so any proxy country returns the same reviews.

tools.name: walmart_search
tools.description: Searches Walmart for `query` and returns the products as JSON: `name`, `price` and `wasPrice`, `rating`, `reviewCount`, `brand`, `seller`, `availability`, `image`, a product `url`, `sponsored`, `unitPrice`, `priceRange`, `promotions`, `fulfillment`, `deliveryAvailable` and `variants`. The response also carries the search's `totalResults`, `pages`, `filters` and `sponsoredProducts`. Sort with `sort`, filter with `min_price`/`max_price`, and collect up to `max_results` across pages. Returns JSON. Billed like an API request; listing plugins bill one unit per result page they fetch, so keep max_results modest.

query.description: What to search, e.g. 'laptop' or 'coffee maker'.

sort.description: Ordering: best_match, price_low, price_high, best_seller, rating_high, new. Default: best_match.

page.description: 1-based page to start from (~40 per page). Default: 1.

max_results.description: How many products to collect across pages. Default: 40.

proxy_country.description: Proxy country the request is sent from (ISO-2, e.g. 'US', 'DE'). Defaults to US.

tools.name: ebay_search
tools.description: Searches any regional eBay marketplace for `keyword` and returns the listings as JSON: `title`, `price` + `currency`, `condition` (with a normalised `conditionCode`), `seller` (username, feedback percentage and score), `shippingCost`, `sold`, `watchers`, `bids`, `image` and a clean item `url`. Filter with `condition`, `listing_type`, `min_price`/`max_price`, `free_shipping`, `seller` or `category`, sort with `sort`, and page with `page`/`page_size` (60, 120 or 240 per page). Set `marketplace` to search a specific site - prices, currency and availability differ between ebay.com, ebay.de, ebay.co.uk and the rest. When eBay finds no exact match it still serves a full page of its own loosely-related suggestions. That case is reported honestly: `exactMatches` is `false` and a `notice` explains it, so those listings are never mistaken for real matches. Returns JSON. Billed like an API request; listing plugins bill one unit per result page they fetch, so keep max_results modest.

keyword.description: Search phrase, e.g. 'iphone 13' or a part number like '1K0953519A'.

marketplace.description: Regional eBay site to search. Prices, currency and availability differ per marketplace. One of: ebay.com, ebay.co.uk, ebay.de, ebay.fr, ebay.it, ebay.es, ebay.nl, ebay.pl, ebay.at, ebay.ch, ebay.be, ebay.ie, ebay.ca, ebay.com.au, ebay.in, ebay.ph, ebay.com.sg, ebay.com.my, ebay.com.hk. Default: ebay.com.

page_size.description: Listings per page - eBay's own page sizes: 60, 120, 240. Default: 60.

condition.description: Item condition filter: new, open_box, refurbished, used, for_parts. Omit for every condition.

sort.description: Ordering: best_match, newly_listed, ending_soon, price_asc, price_desc. Default 'best_match'. Default: best_match.

listing_type.description: Listing format: all, buy_it_now, auction. Default 'all'. Default: all.

min_price.description: Lowest price to include, in the marketplace's currency.

max_price.description: Highest price to include, in the marketplace's currency.

free_shipping.description: Only listings eBay marks as free delivery. Default: false.

seller.description: Restrict the search to one seller's username.

category.description: eBay category id to search inside, e.g. '131090' for vehicle parts and accessories.

proxy_country.description: Proxy country the request is sent from (ISO-2, e.g. 'US', 'DE'). Defaults to a country chosen for the marketplace.

tools.name: google_shopping
tools.description: Runs the Google Shopping vertical (`udm=28`) for `q` and returns the product cards as JSON: `title`, `price`, `currency`, `currencyCode`, `originalPrice`, `discount`, `merchant`, `delivery`, `rating`, `reviewCount`, `image` and Google's own ids for the product (`productId`, `catalogId`, `offerId` - stable across searches, for tracking one product). Set `proxy_country`/`gl` to target a market (prices/merchants are region-specific) and `min_price`/`max_price` to filter. One render returns the first page of products (v1). Note: Google Shopping exposes no per-product URL, so `url` is omitted. `image` is the product's thumbnail URL. Returns JSON. Billed like an API request; listing plugins bill one unit per result page they fetch, so keep max_results modest.

gl.description: Market of search, ISO-2, e.g. 'us', 'de'. Sets prices/merchants. Default: us.

min_price.description: Minimum price filter (whole units, gl currency).

max_price.description: Maximum price filter (whole units, gl currency).

max_results.description: How many products to return (v1: first page). Default: 60.

proxy_country.description: Proxy country the request is sent from (ISO-2, e.g. 'US', 'DE'). Prices/merchants are market-specific.

tools.name: google_local
tools.description: Runs a Google Local (`tbm=lcl`) search for `keyword` and returns up to ~20 businesses as JSON: `name`, `rating`, `reviews`, `price`, `category`, `address`, `phone`, `website`, `hours`, and a top `review_snippet`. `phone` and `website` are null when Google does not render them for that result - service businesses (plumbers, contractors) almost always carry both. Local results are location-sensitive - set `proxy_country` (and optionally `gl`/`hl`) to target a market. Returns JSON. Billed like an API request; listing plugins bill one unit per result page they fetch, so keep max_results modest.

keyword.description: Search phrase, e.g. 'coffee shops in chicago' or 'plumbers near SW1A'.

proxy_country.description: Proxy country the request is sent from (ISO-2, e.g. 'US', 'GB'). Local results are location-sensitive, so pick the country you want results for.

hl.description: Google UI language, e.g. 'en', 'de', 'fr'. Default: en.

gl.description: Google country of search, ISO-2 lowercase, e.g. 'us', 'de'.

tools.name: maps_place_details
tools.description: Returns the full data for one Google Maps place as JSON: `name`, `address` (+ `addressLines`), `phone`, `website`, `rating`, `categories`, `latitude`/`longitude`, `plusCode`, `hours` + `openNow`, `description`, `photo`, `cid`, `featureId`, `googleMapsUrl` and `relatedPlaces`. Identify the place with `place_id` (ChIJ...), a Maps `url`, or a raw `feature_id` (0xHEX:0xHEX). Location-neutral - the feature id resolves the place directly; `proxy_country` defaults to a US proxy to clear Google's consent wall. Returns JSON. Billed like an API request; listing plugins bill one unit per result page they fetch, so keep max_results modest.

url.description: A Google Maps place URL: a /maps/place/... URL, a maps.app.goo.gl share link or a maps?cid= link. The place is read out of it.

feature_id.description: A Maps feature id '0xHEX:0xHEX', e.g. '0x47e66e2964e34e2d:0x8ddca9ee380ef7e0'. Fastest - no resolve step.

hl.description: Google UI language, e.g. 'en', 'de', 'fr'. Default: en.

gl.description: Google country, ISO-2 lowercase, e.g. 'us'. Default: us.

proxy_country.description: Proxy country the request is sent from (ISO-2, e.g. 'US', 'DE'). Defaults to US - an EU country hits Google's consent wall. Default: us.

raw.description: Include the decoded place core array under `raw`. Default: false.

tools.name: google_images
tools.description: Runs the Google Images vertical (`udm=2`) for `q` and returns the image results as JSON. Every result carries `imageUrl` (the full-resolution origin image, not a Google thumbnail; for an image found inside a document such as a PDF, which has no URL of its own, it is Google's thumbnail and `sourcePageUrl` is the document), `sourceDomain` and `googleImagesUrl` (the Google Images viewer link, i.e. the `/imgres?...` URL a browser copies from the result tile), plus `sourcePageUrl`, `title`, `sourceName`, `thumbnailUrl`, `width`, `height` and `fileSize` where available. Set `proxy_country` to target a market: the Google market (`gl`) follows it automatically, and `gl` is only an optional override. `pages` fetches up to 5 result pages of ~100 each; every page fetched is billed as one request. `time_range` (past hour/day/week/month/year) or `date_from`/`date_to` limit the results to images Google found in that period, so a repeated scan returns only what is new. Returns JSON. Billed like an API request; listing plugins bill one unit per result page they fetch, so keep max_results modest.

gl.description: Optional Google market override (ISO-2, e.g. 'us', 'de'). Leave empty and the market follows `proxy_country` ('us' when neither is set). The market, not the proxy country, is what decides which images rank.

pages.description: How many Google Images result pages to fetch (1-5, ~100 results each; Google stops at ~400-500 per query). Each page fetched is billed as one request. Default: 1.

max_results.description: Optional cap on the number of results returned (default: all results of the fetched pages).

proxy_country.description: Proxy country the request is sent from (ISO-2, e.g. 'US', 'DE'). Image results are market-specific.

time_range.description: Only images Google found within this recent period: `hour`, `day`, `week`, `month` or `year` (Google Images' Tools > Time filter). Use it to get just the new results on repeated scans. Cannot be combined with `date_from`/`date_to`.

date_from.description: Only images Google found on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Works alone or with `date_to`; cannot be combined with `time_range`.

date_to.description: Only images Google found on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Works alone or with `date_from`; cannot be combined with `time_range`.

tools.name: youtube_search
tools.description: Searches YouTube for `query` and returns the results as JSON. For each video: `videoId`, `title`, `url`, `channel` (name/id/url), `publishedText`, `viewCount` (+ text), `lengthSeconds` (+ text), `thumbnails`, `descriptionSnippet`, `badges`, `verified` and `isLive`. Filter with `type` (video / channel / playlist / all) and `sort` (relevance / date / views / rating), and collect up to `max_results` across pages. Returns JSON. Billed like an API request; listing plugins bill one unit per result page they fetch, so keep max_results modest.

max_results.description: How many results to collect across pages (~20 per page). Default: 20.

type.description: Result type: video, channel, playlist, movie, all. Default: video.

sort.description: Ordering: relevance, rating, date, views. Default: relevance.

proxy_country.description: Proxy country the request is sent from (ISO-2, e.g. 'US', 'DE'). Defaults to US.

tools.name: youtube_transcript
tools.description: Returns a YouTube video's captions as JSON: timestamped `segments` (`start`, `dur`, `text`) and a joined `text`, plus `availableLanguages`, the picked `language`, `isAutoGenerated`, and the video's `title`, `author` and `lengthSeconds`. Pass a video id or any YouTube video URL; choose a caption language with `lang`. Ideal for LLM/RAG pipelines, subtitles and content analysis. Returns JSON. Billed like an API request; listing plugins bill one unit per result page they fetch, so keep max_results modest.

video.description: Video id (dQw4w9WgXcQ) or any YouTube video URL.

lang.description: Preferred caption language code, e.g. 'en'. Omit for the default/first track. A prefix like 'en' matches 'en-US'.

format.description: Output shape: segments, text. 'segments' returns timestamps; 'text' returns only the joined plaintext. Default: segments.

proxy_country.description: Proxy country the request is sent from (ISO-2, e.g. 'US', 'DE') for the watch page. Defaults to US.

tools.name: zillow_search
tools.description: Searches Zillow for `location` (a city/state or ZIP) and returns the listings as JSON: `price`, `beds`, `baths`, `area`, `address`, `homeType`, `zestimate`, `rentZestimate`, `daysOnZillow`, coordinates, broker and a clean `url`. Filter with `status` (for_sale / for_rent / sold), `min_price`/`max_price`, `beds`, `baths` and `home_type`, sort with `sort`, and collect up to `max_results` across pages. Rental results can include apartment buildings (`isBuilding: true`): they have no `zpid` and carry `lotId`, `buildingName`, a rent range (`price` to `maxPrice`), `units` and `availableUnits` instead. Returns JSON. Billed like an API request; listing plugins bill one unit per result page they fetch, so keep max_results modest.

location.description: City/state or ZIP to search, e.g. 'Austin, TX' or '78704'.

status.description: Listing status: for_sale, for_rent, sold. Default: for_sale.

max_results.description: How many listings to collect across pages (~41 per page). Default: 41.

page.description: 1-based results page to start from. Default: 1.

sort.description: Ordering: newest, price_asc, price_desc, relevant, beds, sqft, lot. Default: newest.

home_type.description: Property type filter: houses, condos, townhomes, multi_family, apartments, manufactured, lots_land. Omit for all.

proxy_country.description: Proxy country the request is sent from (ISO-2, e.g. 'US', 'DE'). Defaults to US.

tools.name: indeed_jobs
tools.description: Searches Indeed for `query` in `location` and returns the job listings as JSON: `title`, `company`, `location`, `salary` (with parsed `min`/`max`), `jobTypes`, `companyRating`, a `snippet`, `datePosted` (YYYY-MM-DD), `sponsored` (Indeed's paid placement) and a clean job `url`. Filter with `country`, `job_type`, `days` (posting age), `remote`, sort with `sort` (`date` returns the collected jobs newest first, sponsored ones included), and collect up to `max_results` across pages. Indeed sits behind Cloudflare + PerimeterX - handled for you. Returns JSON. Billed like an API request; listing plugins bill one unit per result page they fetch, so keep max_results modest.

query.description: What to search, e.g. 'software engineer' or 'nurse'.

country.description: Indeed country site: us, uk, ca, au, in, ie, de, fr, nl, es, it, at, ch, be, pl, se, sg, za, nz, mx. Default: us.

radius.description: Search radius in miles/km around the location.

job_type.description: Job type: fulltime, parttime, contract, internship, temporary.

max_results.description: How many jobs to collect across pages. Default: 30.

start.description: 0-based result offset to start from. Default: 0.

proxy_country.description: Proxy country the request is sent from (ISO-2, e.g. 'US', 'DE'). Defaults to the country's site.

tools.name: trustpilot_reviews
tools.description: Returns a company's Trustpilot profile and reviews as JSON. `company` is the reviewed domain (e.g. `www.nike.com`). The response has a `company` summary (`trustScore`, `totalReviews`, `ratingDistribution` 1-5, `categories`, `contact`) and a `reviews` array - each with `url`, `rating`, `title`, `text`, `verified`, `verificationLevel`, `verificationSource`, `source`, `pending`, `merged`, `author` (name, country, review count, `id`, `image`, `profileUrl`, `reviewsOfThisCompany`), `reply` (the company's response, with dates) and `date` / `experiencedDate` / `updatedDate`. Page with `page`/`pages` (20 reviews per page), and filter with `stars`, `sort` (recency/relevancy), `language`, `date`, `search`, `verified` or `replies`. Returns JSON. Billed like an API request; listing plugins bill one unit per result page they fetch, so keep max_results modest.

company.description: The reviewed company's domain, e.g. 'www.nike.com' or 'nike.com'. A full site URL or a pasted Trustpilot review URL is also accepted.

page.description: 1-based page to start from (20 reviews/page). Default: 1.

pages.description: How many consecutive pages to fetch from `page` onward (20 reviews each). Stops early at the last page. Default: 1.

stars.description: Only reviews with these star ratings (1, 2, 3, 4, 5). Repeatable, e.g. stars=4&stars=5.

sort.description: Ordering: recency, relevancy. Default 'recency' (newest first). Default: recency.

language.description: Review language ISO-2 code (e.g. 'en', 'de') or 'all'. Default 'all'. Default: all.

date.description: Only reviews from a recent window: last30days, last3months, last6months, last12months. Omit for all time.

search.description: Keyword to search within the company's reviews.

verified.description: Only verified reviews (Trustpilot's verified badge). Default: false.

replies.description: Only reviews the company has replied to. Default: false.

proxy_country.description: Proxy country the request is sent from (ISO-2, e.g. 'US', 'DE'). Defaults to a country chosen for the site.

tools.name: booking_hotels
tools.description: Searches Booking.com for `location` and returns the properties as JSON: `name`, `price` (with `checkin`/`checkout`), `reviewScore`, `address`, coordinates, `image` and a hotel `url`. Set `adults`, `children`, `rooms` and `currency`, and collect up to `max_results` across pages. Prices only appear when check-in/check-out dates are given. Returns JSON. Billed like an API request; listing plugins bill one unit per result page they fetch, so keep max_results modest.

location.description: City or place to search, e.g. 'Austin' or 'Paris'.

currency.description: Price currency: USD, EUR, GBP, AUD, CAD, CHF, JPY, CNY, INR, BRL, MXN, PLN, SEK, NOK, DKK, AED, SGD, ZAR, TRY, RUB. Default: USD.

max_results.description: How many properties to collect across pages. Default: 25.

proxy_country.description: Proxy country the request is sent from (ISO-2, e.g. 'US', 'DE').
